subject: ZIP models and goodness of fit statistics

messages.author: eafa26121223327e
messages.subject: ZIP models and goodness of fit statistics
parts:
I'm using ZIP abundance N-mixture models in unmarked to estimate brood abundance at the wetland basin level.  I've run model selection analyses and have a top model which I've assessed model fit for using a parametric bootstrap technique.  Results indicate poor model fit.  What I would like to do (if it is possible and seems rational to someone besides just myself) is see how well the model works at a larger scale.  In other words, I'm wondering if the poor model fit at the basin level is a consequence of low abundance numbers at the basin level (1-3 on average) and a relatively high level of variance... so if I rolled model predictions up to a plot level estimate of abundance, would there be a way to test or assess how 'good' the model does at that level?

KC

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] ZIP models and goodness of fit statistics
parts:
hi Kaylan
 I can't answer your question directly but my sense is that you would have worse-fitting models by aggregating the data. I think disaggregating the data as much as possible should produce the best fit. In your case I guess that would be basin level data. (the reason being that as the sample unit gets small, the data should tend to binary and so there should be no lack of fit induced by the abundance model).
Doesn't hurt to try aggregating though and see what happens.
regards
andy
